paragraphs: Satellites show that the water is going. The cause has to come from evidence on the ground.

The region's wheat and rice are irrigated largely with groundwater pumped from the alluvial aquifers of the Indo-Gangetic plain. Each monsoon puts water back, but the measurements show that over the long term more leaves than returns.

Rodell et al. (2009) checked the other possibilities. Rainfall was close to normal during their study period, and soil moisture, surface water, snow and glaciers could not explain the loss. Citing India's Ministry of Water Resources, they report that groundwater withdrawals exceed recharge in Rajasthan, Punjab and Haryana, and that irrigation accounts for about 95% of the consumption. They conclude that withdrawals for irrigation and other human uses are the likely cause.
Our own analysis measures only the change in stored water. It cannot say who pumped it or why.
